How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed at brookfield village, which was somewhat good price, given the alternatives i found. it was very close to campus, which was nice. however the administration at the place were not nice and generally not very helpful. however the housing options were limited, so i think i got the some of the better options.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: be aware of how far it actually is to the city you're studying in and the options for transport. the public transport if awful in cork

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: mail or in the office

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: i had one introductory course and two master courses. both were fitting level wise, except i have very little experience writing essays, which were the main form of final grading.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: different, the teachers were way more engaged and passionate, which i appreacitated

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: legal research and writing, intellectual property law and criminology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Criminology (LW 6544) the teacher was incredible and the articles we read in class were very nice and had a big variety

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UCC was very big on societies and you were encouraged to be active, which was nice. all student led and very fun

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: all of the societies, there are so many you can definetly find some that match your interests

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: other cities such as dublin, galway, etc. nature: cliffs of moher, ring of kerry - do as many trips as possible

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy, people were friendly and helpfull, however younger than i am used to

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: most parties and social gatherings will proably be with other international students, but through the societies, you can meet more local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: people taking up too much space on the street, the public transport being very unreliable

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Beer, friendly people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: be active in student life, meet international and local students, not just other UCPH students, do as much as possible, but also remember to relax

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: prioritize courses that are interesting and choose ones with essays as final grade over exams

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the feeling of accomplishment being able to plan, execute and enjoy living in a different country on your own

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: prioritizing making friends, that you know arent the most permanent friendsships

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
